title: Ai Trading Bot needed
author: Interesting-Dog-6593
selftext:
If there is anyone out there that is willing to guide me with AI trading bots or possibly have one that currently works. I’m really willing to learn and would love to speak with you about it.

You really don’t have to read this info about my life below, but it will give context. Thank you. 

I’m 34 years old, and I currently work as a teacher’s aide for a large public school district. Lately, I’ve found myself doing a lot of thinking about my future, questioning whether the path I’m currently on will ultimately lead me to the life I truly want.    
I know I have the option of going back to school, becoming a teacher, and potentially earning six figures over the next 10–15 years. There’s absolutely nothing wrong with that path, and I respect the profession. But when I really think about it, I can’t help but feel like there’s something more out there for me. I don’t want to spend the next 15 years simply working toward a comfortable salary while putting the bigger dreams I have for myself and my family on hold.    
My biggest motivation has never really been about having expensive things just for myself. It’s about being in a position where I can take care of the people I love. I want to be able to buy my parents a house, get my dad the dream car he’s always wanted, help my family whenever they need it, and eventually build generational wealth that can benefit the people who come after me.    
I want financial freedom, but I also want time freedom and the ability to live wherever I choose without feeling tied down to a job just to make ends meet.    
The hardest part is that I’ve slowly started losing the passion I once had for working in the school system. It’s not that I don’t enjoy helping children or that I don’t appreciate what I do. It’s that I feel like my current path may not align with the bigger vision I have for my life. And honestly, that feeling has been weighing on me.    
I’ve been looking into trading and different ways to build wealth, and I genuinely believe there may be an opportunity there. But as someone starting from scratch, the amount of information, strategies, courses, and opinions out there is overwhelming. Sometimes I don’t even know where to begin or what information to trust.    
I think about this almost every single day. I’m at a point in my life where I don’t want to waste time chasing the wrong things, but I also don’t want to look back 10 or 15 years from now and regret never taking a chance on myself.    
For those of you who have been in a similar position, especially those who started with little to no experience and eventually built something for themselves:    
Where would you start if you were 34 again? What would you focus on learning? And what advice would you give someone who wants to build real wealth without falling into the trap of chasing every opportunity that comes along?    
I’m not looking for a get-rich-quick scheme. I’m looking for direction, knowledge, and a realistic path toward building a better future for myself and the people I love.    
I know I have the drive and the willingness to learn. I just need help figuring out where to channel that energy.

comments.author: koryuken
comments.body:
Take time, do your research, don't expect things to be handed to you. Stop being lazy and put in some work. With tools like claude code, there's no excuse - you don't need to be a programmer. 

Alpaca for execution.
Polygon for historical data (buy one month of access download all the data locally). 
Claude code - for building and backtesting. 
Oracle VM - free tier, for hosting your vm 24/7 in the cloud. 

There, I literally gave you the recipe, all you need is to put in time.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: anyone offering you a bot that currently works is the first person to walk away from, if it really worked they wouldn't need to sell it. the cheap way to learn is to write down one simple rule and run it on fake money for a few months before a dollar goes in. that's the thing I built Quantradin to do: you type the rule the way you'd explain it to a friend, it tests it on past prices and runs it on paper. free, US stocks and options, quantradin.com. what were you picturing trading?

comments.author: do0fusz
comments.body:
Having a bot gamble for you is a not a bright future.

Do your research, start with: “how many traders lose 90% of their capital within 90 days”.

After that: “how many retail traders can live of their trading without selling courses or indicators”..

Not to pop your dream, but trading isn’t a get rich quick investment.

comments.author: TrenchersAi
comments.body: respect for writing all that out. honest take from someone in this space: there's no bot that reliably prints money, and anyone selling you one that "currently works" is the first red flag to watch for. what does work is learning the basics first, like position sizing, stop losses and why most trades lose, then using bots as a tool on top of that. start with paper trading so you can test strategies with zero real money and see how they hold up for a few weeks. keep your teacher's aide income as your base and only ever trade money you can afford to lose. it's a slow path, but it's the one that doesn't wreck people. happy to point you to free resources if that helps

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
34 is not late, man. If I were you I'd keep the job, learn how to lose small first, and paper trade for a while before trusting anything that trades for you.

Buying your parents a house is a good reason to be patient, not a reason to rush. Good luck, don't give up.

comments.author: Ok-Cake9189
comments.body: The bot is the easy part. The hard part is that there is no strategy that you can give a bot and expect it to reliably, consistently build you wealth over long peruods of time that beats just buy and hold in an index fund. There are lots of strategies that can be profitable for a while amd then tank. Even the latest reasoning models are not able to explain when to expext them to work or to tank. You'd be better off firet leqrning to trade yourself, amd then if you find a strat that worka for you any decent ai can walk you through how to automate it.

comments.author: Fluid_Expression_247
comments.body:
Here's something you need to understand about trading, and life in general. Nobody is going to hand you their golden goose that lays golden eggs. Why would someone give away a trading system that's consistently making them money?

And before you start looking for an AI trading bot, ask yourself whether you even understand what makes a trading strategy profitable. A bot doesn't create an edge. It only automates whatever strategy you give it, profitable or not.

You're talking about building generational wealth and taking care of your family. Those are good goals, but trading is one of the toughest ways to get there. If you're serious about it, start by learning the markets, developing a strategy, and testing whether it actually works. Otherwise, you're setting yourself up to become someone else's source of income.
